## v1.12.0 — Image generation and speech synthesis

Presets can now have illustrations drawn and character lines voiced. AP sends every request from the browser and does not depend on SillyTavern / TauriTavern back-end features, except their CORS proxy when one is needed. Both features are off until the preset declares them and the user turns them on in the new **Media** tab.

### For preset authors
- New manifest fields **`image: true`** and **`speech: true`** (feature flags, like `storylines`). Without them AP shows and requests nothing, and all `image.*` / `speech.*` variables stay off.
- **`kind: image`** structure, written after the content: `{ images: [{ prompt, refs?, ratio?, caption? }] }`, at most `count` per turn (default 1). Dialogue style uses one tag block per image with `<prompt>` `<refs>` `<ratio>` `<caption>` children; imperative style uses an array field. `refs` is only asked for while the connection has reference images.
- **`kind: speech`** inline structure: the model wraps spoken lines in `<speech character="Name">…</speech>` (the tag name is the structure's `tag`). Like annotations, the markup is removed from the message, never shows while streaming, follows edits, and `history: N` puts it back into the last N messages. Provider tags inside a line (`<sigh>`, `(laughs)`, `[whispers]`…) are kept for synthesis and hidden from the displayed text.
- Condition variables: `image.on` `image.auto` `image.api` (`openai` / `gemini` / `novelai` / `openrouter`) `image.prompt` (the connection's prompt type: `tags` / `description` / `instruction`) `image.style` (the connection adds its own style prompt) `image.sfw` (NSFW blocking) `image.refs` (reference images are offered); `speech.on` `speech.auto` `speech.api` `speech.narrator` `speech.characters`. Media is always off on task turns.
- Macros: `{{ap::image::refs}}` (`- <id>: <description>` per reference image offered in the chat: the global ones and those of the chat's character cards), `{{ap::speech::format}}` (short English notes on the inline tags the current speech API understands, empty when it has none), `{{ap::speech::characters}}` (characters with a bound voice in the chat; the model may still voice other characters, and AP asks for their voices).
- CLI: `ap check` warns about media variables or macros without a declaration, declared features without a structure, `image.api` / `image.prompt` / `speech.api` values that do not exist, speech tag clashes, and `minAdvancedPreset` below 1.12.0. `ap preview` gets `--image <api>` (with `--image-prompt <type>` `--image-auto` `--image-style` `--image-sfw` `--image-refs`) and `--speech <api>` (with `--speech-auto` `--speech-narrator` `--speech-characters`), using placeholder macro values.
- User module rule editor: `image.on` / `speech.on` for presets that declare them.
- `window.AdvancedPreset.speech`: read a message's speech lines and listen for changes.

### Image generation
- Connections for **OpenAI** (Image API; reference images through edits), **Gemini** (Interactions API by default, `generateContent` selectable; reference images inline), **NovelAI** (tag prompts, negative prompt) and **OpenRouter** (its Image API for every image model it routes to; Instruction prompts by default, reference images and aspect ratio).
- Per connection: **prompt type**, which tells the preset how to write prompts: *Tags* (comma-separated Danbooru-style tags, for NovelAI and similar), *Description* (one English paragraph describing the image, for SD / Midjourney-like models) or *Instruction* (direct natural-language requirements in any language, for multimodal image models such as GPT Image and Nano Banana); Instruction by default for OpenAI and Gemini, Tags for NovelAI.
- Per connection: style prompt (appended to every request as tags or as a paragraph, following the prompt type; the preset only learns that one exists), NSFW blocking (on by default for OpenAI and Gemini, off for NovelAI).
- Reference images with descriptions (OpenAI / Gemini), **global or bound to a character card**: a card's images are only offered in its chats (every member's in a group chat), so unrelated characters do not get in each other's way. Images can be moved between global and the current chat's cards.
- Image cards below the story: all versions of an image, full-size viewer, regenerate, view and edit the prompt, download, clear generating / error states. With *Generate automatically* off the card shows the prompt and a Generate button. Results follow the reply across swipes.
- Images are stored in IndexedDB, never in settings or chats. The Debug tab can delete generated images that no chat uses any more (every chat is scanned first; nothing is deleted if one cannot be read).

### Speech synthesis
- Connections for **Fish Audio** (model ids, or reference audio sent inline), **ElevenLabs** (premade, account and Voice Library voices; Instant Voice Clone), **MiniMax** (system and account voices; Voice Clone from your own recording), **Gemini** (prebuilt voices, Voice Library, voice replication with a consent recording), **OpenAI** (`/v1/audio/speech`), **DeepSeek** and **OpenRouter** (`/audio/speech`: what a model can do follows the provider in its id, e.g. `elevenlabs/…` gets ElevenLabs' inline tags and `{{ap::speech::format}}`, `fish-audio/…`, `heygen/…` and `bytedance-seed/…` clone from reference audio sent with each request; voices are listed per model). Streaming endpoints are used wherever the API has one, so playback starts early.
- Voices per connection: an optional narrator voice and character → voice bindings, **global or bound to a character card** (a card's bindings only apply in its chats, and win over a global binding of the same name); bindings can be moved between global and the current chat's cards. When a line's character has no voice yet, AP asks you to pick one (once per character) instead of falling back to a default. A voice is a built-in voice, a library voice, an id typed in, or reference audio (with a transcript or consent recording when the API needs one); clones are created on first use. The voice input suggests matching voices as you type, searching the API's voice library when it has one. *Listen* plays a sample.
- Speech lines get their own thin underline, separate from annotations (both can mark the same text); click a line to generate or play it. A player above the story plays the whole message in order (narration too when *Voice narration* is on), with generate all, progress and download. Generated audio can be deleted or regenerated, for one line or the whole message.
- With *Generate automatically* on, the message's audio is prepared as soon as the reply arrives; otherwise when you play it. Audio is cached per connection, voice and text.

### User module groups
- **My modules** can be organized in groups: **single** groups (at most one module on; switching one on switches the others off, all may be off) and **multi** groups. Drag a module's grip to reorder it, move it to another group (collapsed and empty groups included) or out of its group; drag a group's grip to reorder groups. Group headers: fold, rename, single / multi, new module in the group, export, delete (keep the modules or delete them too). The module editor can move a module to another group.
- Export a whole group with its modules; *Export all* includes the groups; imported groups are added as new copies. Export files keep version 1 with an optional `groups` field, so older AP versions still import the modules (ungrouped).
- Presets can ship groups: `userModuleGroups` in `preset.yaml` (names translatable in `locales/<lang>.yaml#userModuleGroups`) and `group:` in the frontmatter of `user-modules/` and `user-module-templates/`. A group is installed the first time a preset version carries it; from then on its name, mode, folding and order are the user's, and a deleted group is not installed again. The group of an installed module counts as its position and stays as the user left it. Exporting the preset with your modules keeps their groups. `ap check` validates group ids, references and that a single group starts with at most one module on; `ap preview` merges bundled modules in their groups.

### Network and CORS proxy
- Media tab → **CORS proxy**: *Auto* (default: direct first, through the proxy once the browser blocks an address, for the rest of the session), *Always* or *Off*.
- Proxy: SillyTavern's `/proxy` (needs `enableCorsProxy: true` in `config.yaml`), TauriTavern's proxy (dev builds), or a custom public proxy (`{url}` placeholder, or the target appended). Clear messages when the proxy is off, missing, or cannot carry the request: SillyTavern's proxy only forwards JSON bodies, so uploads for voice cloning need a direct connection, TauriTavern or a custom proxy.
- Every connection has an *Advanced* section: Base URL, extra or overriding request headers, and a JSON body deep-merged into the built-in one (`null` removes a field).

### Fixes
- Without the CSS Custom Highlight API, repainting annotations could skip or misplace highlights, because the text was located before the old highlight wrappers were removed.

### Other
- Docs: a new guide section on image generation and speech synthesis, reference pages for the new fields, variables and macros, a CORS proxy FAQ; bundled Agent Skills updated.
- **Built-in Petals 7.12.0** (illustrations and voice).

The artifact format is unchanged (3).
- AP before 1.12.0 does not know the `image` / `speech` structure kinds. Presets that use them should set `minAdvancedPreset: 1.12.0`; `ap check` warns.
- Building `image` / `speech` declarations and structures needs CLI 1.12.0.
